blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-migration-1 (Account field renamed in the public API without a BREAKING mark or transition) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it
R-migration-2 (Irreversible DROP COLUMN with no down migration or backup) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.recommendation: Every existing consumer of the public HTTP API that reads `user_name` from the Account JSON gets a missing field (null/undefined or a deserialization error) the moment this ships, with no warning: the release note only says "Changed: Account JSON uses camelCase." Mark the item **BREAKING** in the release note and say what consumers must do (read `userName`); and, since consumers need time, give them a transition — serialize both `user_name` (deprecated) and `userName` for a release, or version the endpoint — then remove the old name in a later change. Add a test of the serialized Account JSON covering the field names.
findings.title: Account field renamed in the public API without a BREAKING mark or transition

findings.evidence: ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN legacy_email;
findings.recommendation: Running migration 0005 deletes every value stored in `users.legacy_email` (the column still holds the data from the 2023 import, even if it is no longer written) and there is no way back: unlike 0004, which ships `0004_accounts.down.sql`, there is no `0005_drop_legacy_email.down.sql`, and the plan names no backup step. Add a down migration that re-adds the column (`ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN legacy_email TEXT;`), and either copy the data out first (e.g. into an archive table, or a documented `pg_dump` of the column) before dropping it, or state in the plan why the data can be lost and how to recover it.
findings.title: Irreversible DROP COLUMN with no down migration or backup
